big_idea: Each LETTER stands for a SOUND. CVC = consonant + vowel + consonant.
learning_intention: We are learning to map letters to sounds in CVC words.
student_learning_goal: I can map letters to sounds in CVC words.
success_criteria: I can SAY the sound a letter makes.
I can SHOW the difference between a letter NAME and its SOUND.
I can BUILD a CVC word using letter cards.
I can READ the word I built.
lesson_specific_materials: 3-Box Sound Box Cards (drawn with marker on index cards)
Letter index cards (lowercase a-z, written in marker; 1 set per pair)
6 picture cards per pair: cat, dog, sun, mat, pin, bag

minds_on.hook: Blendy the Bear: Every letter has a NAME and a SOUND. The name is cee. The SOUND is /c/. Today we map letters to sounds!
minds_on.teacher_script:
Blendy the Bear joins Sounder Sam at the carpet (point to a second stuffed animal, sock, or gesture). 'Reader friends — yesterday Sounder taught us words are made of SOUNDS. Today Blendy adds LETTERS. Each LETTER stands for a SOUND.'

Define. 'A LETTER-SOUND is the SOUND a letter makes — not its name.'

Show name-vs-sound contrast directly. Hold up letter card C. 'NAME is cee. SOUND is /c/. Different!'

Repeat with three letters.
A: name ay, sound /a/. T: name tee, sound /t/. M: name em, sound /m/.

'Blendy says — when we READ, we use the SOUND, not the name.'

Map letters to sound boxes. Place C, A, T cards. 'Sounds: /c/-/a/-/t/. Read: CAT!'

Map a second word. Replace with D, O, G. 'Sounds: /d/-/o/-/g/. Read: DOG!'

'Blendy says — letters in boxes show a CVC word. Read the SOUNDS, then BLEND.'

Class practice. Build SUN and MAT letter-by-letter on a master sound box. Class says each sound, then reads.

Close. 'Sounder + Blendy say — letter NAME and letter SOUND are different. Use the SOUND to read.'
student_actions: Watch Blendy demo letter-name vs sound for C, A, T, M
Read CAT and DOG built in front sound boxes
Read SUN and MAT built letter-by-letter

steps.instruction: Hand each pair a Sound Box Card, a Letter Card set, and 6 picture cards.
For each picture, pairs build the word by placing the matching letter cards in the sound boxes. Then they say the SOUND of each letter and read the whole word.
Pairs trade roles every two pictures.
Stretch: cover one letter and ask the partner to say only the SOUND of that letter (no name).

steps.teacher_prompt: Stop at each pair. Listen for sounds, not names.

differentiation.for_emerging: Use 3 pictures only. Teacher places the first letter as a model.
differentiation.for_extending: Pairs swap one letter to make a new word (CAT → MAT → MAP).
differentiation.for_ell_or_iep: Picture cards with familiar items only; pre-sort the letter set into the 9 letters needed.
differentiation.for_movement_learners: Partners stand and act out each sound — touch head for first, belly for middle, toes for last.

formative_check.what_to_look_for: Five signals: matches letter to sound; says SOUND not name; builds word in sound boxes; reads the whole word; uses slash-notation language when prompted.

discussion_prompts: Show the SOUND of /c/. Now show the NAME of C.
What word did you build today?
consolidation.exit_routine: Each child shares ONE built word: 'I built /__/-/__/-/__/, that's ___.' Class chants 'HOO knows the sounds? YOU do!'

expanded_walkthrough.title: When the child says the letter NAME inside a word — repairing the name-leakage trap at Grade 1
expanded_walkthrough.rationale: Common Grade-1 trap on B2.2: child reads C-A-T by saying 'cee, ay, tee' aloud, then can't blend because the names don't blend into the word. The names actively interfere with the sounds. This builds on the Lesson 1 letter-name trap but is harder because letters are now visible.
expanded_walkthrough.setup: Build activity. Child has placed C, A, T in sound boxes. Reads aloud: 'cee, ay, tee.' Tries to blend: nothing makes sense.
expanded_walkthrough.teacher_script:
Crouch. 'Blendy asks — try the SOUNDS. Each letter has a SOUND. /c/ ... /a/ ... /t/. Now blend: CAT.'

Probe. 'When we read, we say the SOUND. Names are only when we spell out loud or sing the alphabet.'

Generalise. 'Blendy says — to READ, use the SOUND. To NAME the letter, use the name. Different jobs!'

If the child still uses names: cover the picture, point to one letter at a time, ask only for the sound. Then uncover and re-attempt the blend.
expected_student_responses: (Mid) Sounds with prompts, blends with help
(Stretched) 'The name is cee. The sound is /c/. We need the sound.'
common_misconceptions: Letter names blend into words. (Repair: only sounds blend.)
Use whichever — name or sound. (Repair: SOUND for reading.)
recovery_moves: Cover picture, point to one letter, ask 'sound?'.
Demo blending sounds vs names side-by-side: '/c/-/a/-/t/ → CAT. cee-ay-tee → ???'.
If still stuck, return to auditory-only phoneme work for one minute before re-attempting print.

worksheet_brief.purpose: Independent practice of letter-sound mapping in CVC words.

parts_outline.task: Letter-to-sound match: 4 letter cards with 4 phoneme bubbles. Draw a line from each letter to its SOUND.
Build the word: 4 pictures with empty 3-cell sound boxes. Write the letter for each sound.
Read and circle: 3 sound-box words; circle the picture that matches.

expected_image_assets: Sounder Sam and Blendy in worksheet header
4 letter icons + 4 phoneme bubbles for Part 1
